'''Branden Carlson''' (born June 14, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah Utes]].

==Early life and high school career==
Carlson grew up in [[South Jordan, Utah]] and attended [[Bingham High School]].<ref>{{cite web |first=Andrea |last=Urban |title=Former Bingham star settling into big man role for the Utes |url=https://www.fox13now.com/sports/former-bingham-star-settling-into-big-man-role-for-the-utes |website=[[Fox13now.com]] |date=February 18, 2020 |access-date=January 11, 2023}}</ref> Carlson was a consensus four star recruit. He committed to play college basketball at Utah over offers from [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]], [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]], [[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State]], [[UC Davis Aggies men's basketball|UC Davis]], [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara]] and [[Weber State Wildcats men's basketball|Weber State]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Kyle|last=Goon|title=Utah basketball: Bingham big man Branden Carlson picks Runnin' Utes|url=https://archive.sltrib.com/article.php?id=4500749&itype=CMSID|work=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]|date=October 24, 2016|access-date=January 11, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
After serving a two-year mission for [[The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]] (LDS Church), Carlson enrolled at Utah before the start of the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Utah center Branden Carlson got home only in late May, but he's the leader of a 'three-headed' position|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/utah-utes/2019/10/25/utah-center-branden/|work=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]|date=October 25, 2019|access-date=January 12, 2023|last=Kragthorpe|first=Kurt}}</ref> Carlson played in 30 games with 29 starts during his freshman season and averaged 7.0 points, 3.9 rebounds and 1.4 blocks per game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Utah basketball: Branden Carlson didn't let COVID-19 keep him down|url=https://www.deseret.com/2022/2/16/22936479/utah-basketball-branden-carlson-doggedly-determined-craig-smith-runnin-utes-stanford-cal-pac-12|work=[[Deseret News]]|date=February 16, 2022|access-date=January 11, 2023|last=Drew|first=Jay}}</ref> He averaged 9.4 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.7 blocks as a sophomore.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jay|last=Drew|title=Branden Carlson reflects on his Runnin' Utes career|url=https://www.deseret.com/2023/3/7/23626423/utah-basketball-branden-carlson-future-ahead-of-pac-12-tourney|work=[[Deseret News]]|date=March 7, 2023|access-date=January 11, 2023}}</ref> Carlson averaged 13.6 points, 6.1 rebounds and 1.6 blocks and was named second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12 Conference]] as a junior.<ref>{{cite web|first=Trevor|last=Allen|title=Instant Replay: Utah Basketball Center Branden Carlson Throws Down Impressive Dunk|url=https://kslsports.com/488237/instant-replay-utah-basketball-center-branden-carlson-throws-down-impressive-dunk/|website=[[KSL-TV|KSLSports.com]]|date=June 16, 2022|access-date=January 11, 2023}}</ref> 

He averaged 16.4 points, 7.5 rebounds and 2.0 blocks per game as a senior and was named first-team All-Pac-12.<ref>{{cite web|title=Utah Runnin' Utes basketball standout Branden Carlson will return to school|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/utah-utes/2023/05/31/runnin-utes-basketballs-branden/|work=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]|date=May 31, 2023|access-date=January 11, 2023|last=Vejar|first=Alex}}</ref> Carlson considered entering the [[2023 NBA draft]], but ultimately decided to utilize the extra year of eligibility granted to college athletes who played in the 2020 season due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and return to Utah for a fifth season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Branden Carlson is returning for the 2023–24 season|url=https://www.deseret.com/2023/5/31/23744271/branden-carlson-returning-to-utah-utes-basketball-for-2023-24-season|work=[[Deseret News]]|date=May 31, 2023|access-date=January 12, 2023}}</ref> In his final year, he averaged 17.0 points, 6.6 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.5 blocks per game,<ref name="TorontoRaptors2w">{{cite web|first=Brandon|last=Judd|title=Branden Carlson joins Toronto Raptors on two-way contract|url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2024/06/27/branden-carlson-two-way-contract-toronto-raptors/|work=[[Deseret News]]|date=June 28, 2024|access-date=June 29, 2024}}</ref> and made the [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|First-team All-Pac-12]] for the second time. Carlson became the all-time blocks leader for Utah during a home loss to [[2023–24 Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball team|Arizona State]],<ref>{{cite web|first=Michelle|last=Bodkin|title=Branden Carlson Makes More History As A Runnin’ Ute|url=https://kslsports.com/511110/branden-carlson-blocks-leader-utah-2024/|website=KSL Sports|date=February 10, 2024|access-date=June 28, 2024}}</ref> eventually finishing the season with 241 blocks. In that year's [[2024 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]], Carlson averaged 16.8 points, 5.0 rebounds and 1.8 blocks over four tournament games, with Utah eventually falling in the semifinals to [[2023–24 Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball team|Indiana State]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Brandon|last=Judd|title=What Utah said about its run to the NIT semifinals|url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2024/04/03/what-stood-out-from-utahs-nit-run-utes-mens-basketball/|work=[[Deseret News]]|date=April 4, 2024|access-date=June 29, 2024}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Raptors 905 (2024)===
After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Carlson signed a two-way contract with the [[Toronto Raptors]] on July 4, 2024, joining former Ute [[Jakob Pöltl]].<ref name="TorontoRaptors2w"/><ref>{{cite web|title=RAPTORS SIGN CARLSON TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-carlson-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 4, 2024|access-date=July 5, 2024}} </ref> However, he was waived on October 19, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|title=RAPTORS WAIVE THREE, CONVERT BATTLE TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-waive-three-convert-battle-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}}</ref> On October 28, he joined [[Raptors 905]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RAPTORS 905 FINALIZES TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=https://raptors905.gleague.nba.com/news/raptors-905-finalizes-training-camp-roster-3|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2024}}</ref> Carlson played four preseason games with the Raptors, averaging 5.3 minutes per game. He averaged 1.8 points, 1.3 rebounds and 0.5 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Branden Carlson 2024-25 Preseason Game Log |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4592435/type/nba/year/2025 |publisher=ESPN |access-date=11 February 2025}}</ref>

===Oklahoma City Thunder / Blue (2024–2026)===
On November 16, 2024, after the injuries of [[Isaiah Hartenstein]], [[Chet Holmgren]] and [[Jaylin Williams (basketball, born 2002)|Jaylin Williams]], Carlson signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Branden Carlson|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-carlson-241116|website=NBA.com|date=November 16, 2024|access-date=November 16, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder signing Branden Carlson to boost hobbled frontcourt|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/42424658|website=ESPN.com|date=November 16, 2024|access-date=November 16, 2024|last=Charania|first=Shams|author-link=Shams Charania}}</ref> Throughout his rookie season, he was [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Oklahoma City Blue Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Oklahoma-City-Blue/38/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 21, 2024}}</ref> On January 7, 2025, he was waived by the Thunder.<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Thunder Cut Branden Carlson|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/01/thunder-cut-branden-carlson.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=January 7, 2025|access-date=January 7, 2025}}</ref> Three days later, he signed a 10-day contract with the Thunder.<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Branden Carlson to 10-day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-carlson-250110|website=NBA.com|date=January 10, 2025|access-date=January 10, 2025}}</ref> Against the [[2024–25 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]] on January 16, Carlson recorded 11 points and 4 rebounds, making 3 three-pointers off the bench in a blowout win.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Almanza |first=Clemente |title=How Branden Carlson stole the spotlight in Thunder's 134-114 win over Cavaliers |url=https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/thunder/2025/01/17/branden-carlson-steals-spotlight-in-thunder-134-114-win-over-cavaliers/77774834007/ |access-date=2025-06-14 |website=okcthunderwire.usatoday.com |language=en-US|date=2025-01-17}}</ref> On January 22, he signed another 10-day contract with the Thunder.<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Branden Carlson to Second 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-carlson-250122|website=NBA.com|date=January 22, 2025|access-date=January 22, 2025}}</ref> On February 6, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Thunder and the Blue.<ref>{{cite web |last=Styles |first=Ryan |title=OKC Thunder Ink Branden Carlson to Two-Way Pact |url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/news/okc-thunder-ink-branden-carlson-to-two-way-pact |website=Sports Illustrated |publisher=SI.com |date=February 7, 2025 |access-date=February 6, 2025}}</ref> In Oklahoma City's final regular-season game against the [[2024-25 New Orleans Pelicans season|New Orleans Pelicans]], Carlson recorded a season-high 26 points, 10 rebounds and 3 blocks in a double-digit win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-13 |title=OKC Thunder Ensnares New Orleans Pelicans in Season Finale |url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/news/okc-thunder-ensnares-new-orleans-pelicans-in-season-finale |access-date=2025-06-14 |website=SI.com |language=en-US|last=Baca|first=Ethan}}</ref> Carlson finished his rookie season an NBA champion when the Thunder defeated the Indiana Pacers in seven games in the [[2025 NBA Finals]].

On July 8, 2025, Carlson re-signed with Oklahoma City on a two-way contract.<ref>{{cite web | last=Gemes | first=Chase | title=Branden Carlson Returning to Thunder on Two-Way Contract | website=SI.com | date=2025-07-09 | url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/onsi/news/branden-carlson-return-to-thunder-good-for-both-sides | access-date=2025-12-07}}</ref> On April 12, 2026, Carlson tied a career–high in points with 26, also chipping in 10 rebounds, five blocks, two steals and one assist as part of a 135–103 loss to the [[2025–26 Phoenix Suns season|Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Thunder's Branden Carlson: Double-double in defeat|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/thunders-branden-carlson-double-double-in-defeat/|access-date=April 25, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}}</ref> Carlson made 32 appearances for Oklahoma City during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], posting averages of 3.8 points, 3.0 rebounds, and 0.7 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Branden Carlson 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4592435/branden-carlson|access-date=August 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

=== Portland Trail Blazers (2026–present) ===
On July 1, 2026, Carlson signed a one-year, $2.5 million contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Portland Trail Blazers Sign Branden Carlson |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/portland-trail-blazers-sign-branden-carlson |access-date=2026-07-01 |publisher=NBA.com|date=2026-07-01}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Carlson is a member of [[The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]]. He served a two-year mission for the church in [[Manchester]], England.<ref>{{cite web|title=Utah basketball center Branden Carlson is shining, aided by summer with AAU team|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/utah-utes/2020/02/12/utah-center-branden/|work=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]|date=February 12, 2020|access-date=January 11, 2023}}</ref>

Carlson married Maddy Woolf in the summer of 2020.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Drew |first1=Jay |title=Branden Carlson reflects on his Runnin’ Utes career — which might not be close to over |url=https://www.deseret.com/2023/3/7/23626423/utah-basketball-branden-carlson-future-ahead-of-pac-12-tourney/ |website=[[Deseret News]]|publisher=The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints |access-date=2025-01-17|date=2025-03-07}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Drew |first1=Jay |title=Branden Carlson on why he came back and his expectations for rebuilt Runnin’ Utes |url=https://www.deseret.com/2023/6/7/23751771/utah-runnin-utes-basketball-nil-deals-branden-carlson-craig-smith-cole-bajema-lawson-lovering-ncaa/ |website=[[Deseret News]]|access-date=2025-01-17|date=2023-06-07}}</ref> His father, Bryan Carlson, played basketball at [[Chico State Wildcats|Chico State]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Branden Carlson Nationality |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/basketball/branden-carlson-nationality |website=Sportskeeda |access-date=7 February 2025}}</ref> and his brother, Devin Carlson, plays forward for [[Salt Lake Community College]]'s basketball team.<ref>{{cite web |title=Roster |url=https://slccbruins.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster |publisher=Salt Lake Community College |access-date=7 February 2025}}</ref>
